brief.headline: Former Blackstone executive’s Town Lane raises $1.9bn for second real estate fund
bullets: Fundraising: Town Lane Management, the real estate investment firm founded by former Blackstone executive Tyler Henritze, has raised $1.9bn for its second fund, exceeding its fundraising target by more than 25%, according to a report by Bloomberg.

M&A & Buyouts: Universal Music Group has held preliminary discussions with private equity firms including Apollo Global Management, TPG and Blackstone over a potential take-private transaction, although the talks have not progressed into a formal sale process, according to a report by Bloomberg.

Private Credit: Blackstone-backed data centre operator QTS Realty Trust is seeking to raise approximately $800m through a private debt placement, as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure drives further financing activity across private credit markets, according to a report by Bloomberg.
AI & Technology: They also discuss how they built one of the most influential media companies of the last decade and lessons from their new book, Simplify: Do 50% More with 50% Less.
Real Estate: TKO wants to buy a hotel portfolio roughly four times the size of its own.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,676.77 (up 0.7% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 18.4, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.00% (up 4 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.32 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.30%, near long-run norms (down 8 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: Blackstone-backed QTS seeks $800m private debt financing

items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.30%, near long-run norms (down 8 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 26.)
